sources.title: Devangana Desai, Khajuraho (2000), history and temple studies
sources.note: Original scholarly book read in full-text mirror, especially pp. 9-11 and genealogy pp. 89-90. Mirror hosts the book, not an independent source. Broad reign ranges are approximate; uncertain architectural patronage is not treated as proven.

sources.title: UNESCO, Khajuraho Group of Monuments
sources.note: Direct official Outstanding Universal Value: dynasty apogee 950-1050, architecture, sculpture subjects, Hindu/Jain affiliation, conservation.

sources.title: F. Kielhorn, Inscriptions from Khajuraho and Chandella records, Epigraphia Indica I (1892)
sources.note: Original ASI volume downloaded. Printed p. 129 closing line and p. 135 translation visually checked, PDF pages 156 and 162. P. 134 verse 47; pp. 135-136 Pahilla record and re-engraving caveat. Mau inscription pp. 195-207 read in same-edition transcription at https://jainqq.org/booktext/Epigraphia_Indica_Vol_01/032555 . All uses counted together.

sources.title: Indian Museum, Kolkata, Mother fondling her child
sources.note: Direct museum-authored object description, ca. tenth-eleventh century, Khajuraho provenance, 90 x 33 cm. Costume and hairstyle are observations of this sculpture, not universal practices.

sources.title: Cleveland Museum of Art, Lovers (Mithuna), 1982.64
sources.note: Original museum record and readable print view https://www.clevelandart.org/print/art/1982.64 checked: 1000s, Khajuraho, sandstone, 74 cm; interpretation of idealized lovers as auspicious.

sources.title: Census of India 2011, District Census Handbook: Mahoba, Part A
sources.note: Direct PDF failed; original indexed Mahoba town entry read. Reproducible query: "Mahoba" "Rahila sagar" "massive embankments". Supports valley embankments and granite steps at Kirat Sagar, not measured medieval water quality.

sources.title: Ministry of Tourism, Incredible India: Mahoba
sources.note: Original indexed text read; direct page fails. Query: site:incredibleindia.gov.in "Mahoba" "Madan Sagar". Attributes Rahila Sagar, Kirat Sagar and Madan Sagar to rulers and gives their approximate reign ranges.

sources.title: George F. Dales, South Asia’s Earliest Writing, Penn Museum Expedition
sources.note: Direct article read. Closing discussion and illustration concern tenth-eleventh-century Khajuraho sculpture of a woman writing with a conical stylus; wax tablet explicitly tentative. Its separate Harappan analogy is not used here.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India, Indian Archaeology 1988-89: A Review
sources.note: Direct original ASI report, printed p. 39 / PDF page 46, section 48, Excavation at Khajuraho. Report distinguishes Post-Gupta/Pratihara and Chandela phases but does not assign every small find to one phase.

sources.title: Sisirkumar Mitra, The Early Rulers of Khajuraho
sources.note: Original scholarly monograph at IGNCA; direct fetch fails, targeted indexed original read. Query: site:ignca.gov.in/Asi_data/15563.pdf "Trailokyavarman" yields p. 137, later local rule and queen Kalyanadevi water works. VS 1317 is not CE 1317; public passage deliberately says thirteenth century.

proposedOverrides.name: Chandelas of Bundelkhand
proposedOverrides.summary: Bundelkhand’s Chandela rulers supported Khajuraho’s temples and a wider landscape of forts and waterworks.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Exact indexed identity only. Broad north-central Indian polygon is retained as imported map coverage, not certified as the boundary of a single reign. Historical narrative explicitly extends earlier and later than the imported 1100-1200 interval; no related aliases added.
batchIdentityNotes.limitations: No household sanitation or clinical medicine claim established. Sculpture is treated as imagery, not a population survey. Pahilla record is a later re-engraving of an earlier grant; original-language sample instead uses the separately attested Lakshmana inscription.
